title: CoreWeave: A pro forma
excerpt: A multi-dimensional sensitivity analysis of CoreWeave, inspired by the phase diagram of physics. Can renting GPUs by the hour pay off the debt that bought them?

What the 10-Q does not tell us

Fig. 1 · One GPU, one loan, rented by the hour

Phase diagram

Move the levers and watch which of three states the GPU lands in. Like water, it changes state when squeezed: price is the pressure, the cost of money is the heat.

Melt path: the same deal signed one, two, three years later

Swipe sideways to see the whole chart →

Solid

Profitable: rent repays the loan and owners beat their target return.

Liquid

Lenders paid, owners short: the loan is repaid, but owners earn less than their target.

Anxious

Needs new financing: rent banked falls behind the loan payments. New capital or a refinancing has to fill the gap.

Click or drag on the diagram to move the two levers on its axes. All other levers stay where the sliders are. The three small diagrams are the same GPU seen along each pair of the three big levers. The melt path shows on price against rentable life; CoreWeave’s debt shows on the two Fed-rate views.

Fig. 2 · Rental economics of one GPU-hour

Where each rental dollar goes

Which GPU? CoreWeave’s fleet average, not one make or model.

  • Rented like an Nvidia H100: an hour when new.
  • Costs to buy and install: a blend of H100s (about $37,000) and newer Blackwell GPUs ($60,000 to $77,000).

Rent per GPU-hour, averaged over the GPU’s rentable life. Percentages are shares of the first bar.

Fig. 3 · Which lever matters most

Longer bar, stronger lever

Lever at its better end Lever at its worse end Repayment line: loan cover 1.00× Loan cover now

Each row moves one lever alone across a range and holds the rest at the slider values. The ranges: price $2.46 to $3.69, the H100 contract prices on the price sheet. Fleet hours earning rent 59% to 82%, the band above the phase diagram. Rentable life 3 to 6 years, the lives the industry argues over. The rest are my assumptions: installed cost $40,000 to $60,000, yearly price fall 0% to 15%, Fed rate and lender’s margin 1.5 points either side, and running costs 25% either side. “Better” means a higher price, a fuller fleet or a longer life, and a lower cost or rate. Loan share, loan length and the owners’ required return are left out: they are choices, not risks.

Cumulative dollars per GPU. New financing is needed the first year rent banked ends below loan payments due.
